messages.subject: Re: Bar Chart Help
messages.subject_clean: Bar Chart Help
messages.body_plain:
Hi Br,

>The problem I am facing is "outlier values" distorting the axis.
>Specifically. "Delta" values of 4215 and -15.

My only real suggestion is to not express them as deviations from the
mean.  That handles the lower end (if you want the means in there, maybe
put them in as horizontal lines?). You're stuck with the top end being
skewed. Surely that is the whole point of the Premier League's existence.

Looking at the data I did wonder why the overall average for the 2014-15
season was less than all of the values for the divisions.

>>And lastly any suggestions on how to spice up the graph to make it look
>>like an "infographic"

Well you might mess about with plotting them as points with the size
determined by the wage. (maybe x as level, y as season; or the same y for
both seasons with different colours for seasons, a bit of jitter (?) and
alpha < 1).

Ron.

messages.subject: Re: Increase the size of the map and centre name of places
messages.subject_clean: Increase the size of the map and centre name of places
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

>I am facing a problem on enlarging the below map and placing names at the
>centre of polygons.

Decide how big you want your graphic to be, and set that size when opening
the device to write it to. Then optimise the font sizes etc for that
graphic size.

What is your problem with the name placement? That they overlap other
names/other polygons? That they aren't at the centre of all the polygons?
You will probably need to tweak the positions manually (but centroid
rather than a mean x and y might be a better starting point), and maybe
rotate some of them. Take a look at ?geom_text

>Here is the code I used

But there is no data, so nobody can play with it to come up with a
solution. And theme_nothing, what is that? A reproducible example would be
helpful, with bits that aren't relevant to the problem removed.

Ron.

messages.body_plain:
​Here is full code and the data hopefully it will help.

library(maps)
library(maptools)
library(sp)
library(rgdal)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) # a for making pretty plots
library(RColorBrewer) # a package that has some pretty colors for the maps
library(ggmap)
library(gridExtra)
## read the shapefile
sl_district <- readShapePoly("~/downloads/SLE_adm_shp/SLE_adm3.shp")
## Select Kaialhun district
Kailahun<-subset(sl_district,NAME_2=="Kailahun") # make sure the name and the content of the columns are spelled correctly
plot(Kailahun) # Plots the district map

## Set the working directory to desktop
setwd("~/Desktop/gis")
# set directory
td <- ("~/Desktop/gis")
## Write the shapefile to working directory
writeOGR(Kailahun, dsn= "td", layer="Kailahun", driver="ESRI Shapefile")## this one worked
## Read the shapefile from the directory
Kailahun <- readOGR(dsn="td", layer="Kailahun")
str(Kailahun)
class(Kailahun)
names(Kailahun)
print(Kailahun$NAME_3)
kaichief <- length(kailahun$NAME_3)
kailahun.df <- fortify(Kailahun,region="NAME_3")
kailahun.df <- rename(kailahun.df,x=Long,y=Lat)
head(kailahun.df)

## Label Chiefdoms
kai <- aggregate(cbind(long, lat) ~ id, data=kailahun.df, FUN=function(x) mean(range(x)))
## plot the map
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = kailahun.df,
               aes(x=long , y=lat , group = group),
               color = "burlywood1", size =0.25) +
  coord_map()+
  scale_fill_distiller(name="Cumulative", palette = "RdYlGn") +
  theme_nothing(legend = TRUE) +
  labs(title="Cumulative maternal deaths in Kailahun from Week 1 to 7") +
  geom_text(data=kai,aes(long, lat, label = id),colour="gold2",size=2.5, fontface="bold")​

Warm Regards

Yuster Ronoh

WHO Sierra Leone

messages.body_plain:
Dear ggploters,

It seems to me that something has happened to the labeller function in ggplot.  I have used the following labeller code many times but today it provides the following error message:

trial_labeller <- function(var, value){
  value <- as.character(value)
  if (var=="Trial") {
    value[value=="A"] <- "2011"
    value[value=="B"]   <- "2012"
  }
  return(value)
}

Error in labeller(label_df) :
  argument "value" is missing, with no default

I have checked older scripts that have always worked perfectly and the same error message is now received.  I have updated my ggplot package to no effect.

I provide a MRE below.  Anyone else had experience of this?

Thanks,

Felix

messages.subject: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?
messages.subject_clean: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?
messages.body_plain:
I'm (foolishly) trying to write a stat that will draw a smooth path that encloses a specified set of x,y points (if anyone already has a solution for this please let me know!!).  One of my current problems is that for some of the computations I want to do, it would be extremely useful to know the aspect ratio of the plot -- this would be similar to the problem of drawing a circle on a plot regardless of the x/y values, as in

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/6862742/draw-a-circle-with-ggplot2

I'm afraid, though, that beyond the narrow technical difficulty of "how do I recover this information within the scope of a stat?", this may be harder -- because the aspect ratio may not even be defined at the time the stat is computed.  I might be better off trying to construct my path as a grob and use annotation_custom to add it <http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/annotation_custom.html>, but I'd ideally like to be able to enclose/annotate *different* sets of points in different facets ...

My current, not entirely workable strategy for what I'm calling StatEncircle is:

   - find convex-hull of points to be encircled
   - expand convex hull by pushing points away from the centroid (this is where I need the aspect ratio)
   - use graphics::xspline to construct a smooth curve through the points (this part also needs work ...)

Any input is welcome.

stairstepn <- function( data, direction="hv", yvars="y" ) {
  direction <- match.arg( direction, c( "hv", "vh" ) )
  data <- as.data.frame( data )[ order( data$x ), ]
  n <- nrow( data )

  if ( direction == "vh" ) {
    xs <- rep( 1:n, each = 2 )[ -2 * n ]
    ys <- c( 1, rep( 2:n, each = 2 ) )
  } else {
    ys <- rep( 1:n, each = 2 )[ -2 * n ]
    xs <- c( 1, rep( 2:n, each = 2))
  }

  data.frame(
    x = data$x[ xs ]
    , data[ ys, yvars, drop=FALSE ]
    , data[ xs, setdiff( names( data ), c( "x", yvars ) ), drop=FALSE ]
  )
}

stat_stepribbon <-

  function(mapping = NULL, data = NULL, geom = "ribbon", position = "identity", inherit.aes = TRUE) {
    ggplot2::layer(
      stat = Stepribbon, mapping = mapping, data = data, geom = geom,
      position = position, inherit.aes = inherit.aes
    )
  }

StatStepribbon <-
  ggproto("stepribbon", Stat,
          compute_group = function(., data, scales, direction = "hv", yvars = c( "ymin", "ymax" ), ...) {

            stairstepn( data = data, direction = direction, yvars = yvars )

          },
          required_aes = c( "x", "ymin", "ymax" )
  )

messages.subject_clean: Changing Colors on a ggplot2 Scatterplot
messages.body_plain:
Hello all!
I'm attempting to modify some existing code that was originally from the question found here (http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/76999/simulating-longitudinal-lognormal-data-in-r), and used to demonstrate scatterplots in R at the following website: <https://hopstat.wordpress.com/2014/10/30/my-commonly-done-ggplot2-graphs/>

It's a simple and stupid question, but I've been struggling with it all morning. The following code gives a nice black and white scatterplot. I want to modify the code to make the lines a very light gray.

    library(MASS)
    library(nlme)
    library(plyr)
    library(ggplot2)

    ### set number of individuals
    n <- 200

    ### average intercept and slope
    beta0 <- 1.0
    beta1 <- 6.0

    ### true autocorrelation
    ar.val <- .4

    ### true error SD, intercept SD, slope SD, and intercept-slope cor
    sigma <- 1.5
    tau0  <- 2.5
    tau1  <- 2.0
    tau01 <- 0.3

    ### maximum number of possible observations
    m <- 10

    ### simulate number of observations for each individual
    p <- round(runif(n,4,m))

    ### simulate observation moments (assume everybody has 1st obs)
    obs <- unlist(sapply(p, function(x) c(1, sort(sample(2:m, x-1,
    replace=FALSE)))))

    ### set up data frame
    dat <- data.frame(id=rep(1:n, times=p), obs=obs)

    ### simulate (correlated) random effects for intercepts and slopes
    mu  <- c(0,0)
    S   <- matrix(c(1, tau01, tau01, 1), nrow=2)
    tau <- c(tau0, tau1)
    S   <- diag(tau) %*% S %*% diag(tau)
    U   <- mvrnorm(n, mu=mu, Sigma=S)

    ### simulate AR(1) errors and then the actual outcomes
    dat$eij <- unlist(sapply(p, function(x) arima.sim(model=list(ar=ar.val),
    n=x) * sqrt(1-ar.val^2) * sigma))
    dat$yij <- (beta0 + rep(U[,1], times=p)) + (beta1 + rep(U[,2], times=p)) *
    log(dat$obs) + dat$eij

    dat = ddply(dat, .(id), function(x){
      x$alpha = ifelse(runif(n = 1) > 0.9, 1, 0.1)
      x$grouper = factor(rbinom(n=1, size =3 ,prob=0.5), levels=0:3)
      x
    })
    tspag = ggplot(dat, aes(x=obs, y=yij)) +
      geom_line() + guides(colour=FALSE) + xlab("Observation Time Point") +
      ylab("Y")
    spag = tspag + aes(colour = factor(id))
    spag
    bwspag = tspag + aes(group=factor(id))
    bwspag

I've tried scale_colour_manual, I've tried defining the color within the aes statement on the bwspag line...no luck. I'm relatively inexperienced with R. I appreciate any assistance! The black and white graph generated is attached. I'm using RStudio...also tried in R with no luck.

messages.body_plain:
OK, next stupid question.

The code below works fine with a dummy (unused) new default aesthetic called 'xx' and set to a value of 2. If I make the minimal change of setting the default value for xx to "a", or many other things (other strings, 0, positive integers, positive floats), it works.  If I set it to -1 or (my current working hypothesis) *any other value that requires any evaluation/parsing by R* (-1 requires evaluation because it is really (unary minus(1))), I get

Error in rep(value[[k]], length.out = n) :
  attempt to replicate an object of type 'language'

I'm guessing (again, just my current working hypothesis) that there is some kind of magic lazy stuff going on in the guts of ggproto/ggplot that stops this from working.

Am I being an idiot?
Does this constitute a bug or just an infelicity?
Any thoughts for a workaround (a really, really ugly case that I just thought of, since I need the shape parameter to be able to vary from -1 to 1, is to pass the shape as a value on [0,2] and then subtract 1 once I get inside the function ...)

=========
library("ggplot2")
library("grid")

g0 <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point()
.

GeomXSpline <- ggproto("GeomXSpline", Geom,
  required_aes = c("x", "y"),
  default_aes = aes(colour = "black", xx=2),
  draw_key = draw_key_point,

  draw_panel = function(data, panel_scales, coord) {
    coords <- coord$transform(data, panel_scales)
    print(head(coords))
    grid::xsplineGrob(
      coords$x, coords$y,
      gp = grid::gpar(col = coords$colour)
    )
  }
)

geom_xspline <- function(mapping = NULL, data = NULL, stat = "identity",
                         position = "identity", na.rm = FALSE, show.legend = NA,                               inherit.aes = TRUE, ...) {
  layer(
    geom = GeomXSpline, mapping = mapping,  data = data, stat = stat,
    position = position, show.legend = show.legend, inherit.aes = inherit.aes,
    params = list(na.rm = na.rm, ...)
  )
}

g0 + geom_xspline(colour="red")

messages.subject_clean: Adding ggplotGrob at a predefined location
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I posted this question <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/35736896/ggplot-a-panel-of-histograms-with-histograms-as-subplots/35737909?noredirect=1#comment59175590_35737909> at stack overflow and got a great answer. Essentially it is about adding an inset plot to each facet created by ggplot2 with facet_grid.
The solution in the answer is to use ggplotGrob but in the answer the location of each inset is hard-coded. In my real data I'm using this graphing strategy for different data sets with different numbers of facets, and therefore was wondering if there's a way to predetermine the x-location of the inset plots according to how many facets are plotted in the main plot.

Thanks a lot,
rubi

It is not exactly what you wanted, but check whether this will do the trick

plot1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x=y)) + geom_histogram(colour="black", fill="white") + facet_grid(. ~ site)
plot2 <- ggplot(df, aes(site_subjects)) + geom_bar() + facet_grid(. ~ site)
library("gridExtra")
grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(plot1, plot2), ncol = 1)

Regards,
Anant

#REQUIRES A FUNCTION...from Cookbook...
summarySE <- function(data=NULL, measurevar, groupvars=NULL, na.rm=FALSE,
                      conf.interval=.95, .drop=TRUE) {
  require(plyr)

  # New version of length which can handle NA's: if na.rm==T, don't count them
  length2 <- function (x, na.rm=FALSE) {
    if (na.rm) sum(!is.na <http://is.na>(x))
    else       length(x)
  }

  # This does the summary. For each group's data frame, return a vector with
  # N, mean, and sd
  datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
                 .fun = function(xx, col) {
                   c(N    = length2(xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     sd   = sd     (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm)
                   )
                 },
                 measurevar
  )

  # Rename the "mean" column
  datac <- rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))

  datac$se <- datac$sd / sqrt(datac$N)  # Calculate standard error of the mean

  # Confidence interval multiplier for standard error
  # Calculate t-statistic for confidence interval:
  # e.g., if conf.interval is .95, use .975 (above/below), and use df=N-1
  ciMult <- qt(conf.interval/2 + .5, datac$N-1)
  datac$ci <- datac$se * ciMult

  return(datac)
}

I haven't looked at it, but I assume the geom_xspline is the same
(mine just wraps grid::xsplineGrob).  The fun thing in my code is not
geom_xspline, but geom_encircle, which uses a combination of a convex
hull, inflation away from the centroid, and a spline interpolation to
create a smooth path around a specified set of points.

messages.subject_clean: A line graph with one sided error bars and a table on the x-axis
messages.body_plain:
I would like to create a line graph with two features that I don't see in the books.  I am barely past the beginner stage in R, and freely admit that I may be looking in the wrong places. Pointers would be much appreciated.

The graph I would like to produce has two series with lines and points. I want upper error bars on one series, and lower error bars on the other. I can make the error bars, but I get undesired whiskers at the data points.

I would also like to have a fairly complex table below the x-axis. This table contains counts that come from the data. Preferably the table would be tied directly to the data, so that I don't have to type the actual number.

Such a graph is straightforward in Excel or PowerPoint, but the resolution is really bad when it gets into a journal. The graph in the link below was created by me that way.  My goal is to do better, but I can't (yet) get everything done in R.

The graph I have in mind is figure 2 at the link. http://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1200384#t=article

messages.body_plain:
Labeller functions have changed in ggplot2-2.x.y; to see the current
help page for version 2.1.0, go here:
http://docs.ggplot2.org/dev/labeller.html

It's not exactly clear to me what you wanted, but if the idea is to
print "Label" when class = A and "Label 2" when class = B, then this
works:

library(ggplot2)     # version 2.1.0

DATA <- structure(list(NO = c(3L, 8L, 2L, 1L), ITEM = structure(1:4,
.Label = c("W",
"X", "Y", "Z"), class = "factor"), CLASS = structure(c(1L, 1L,
2L, 2L), .Label = c("A", "B"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("NO",
"ITEM", "CLASS"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -4L
))

p <- ggplot(data=DATA, aes(x=ITEM, y =NO))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity")

# In ggplot v. 2.0.0 +, you can use a labeller function with facet_wrap():

p <- ggplot(data=DATA, aes(x=ITEM, y =NO))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity")

my_labs <- c(A = "Label", B = "Label 2")
p + facet_wrap(~ CLASS,
                      labeller = labeller(CLASS = my_labs),
                      scales = "free_x")

The functionality for facet labels has changed enough that it's
probably worth re-educating yourself about its (new) capabilities.

Dennis

help page for version 2.1.0, go here:
http://docs.ggplot2.org/dev/labeller.html

It's not exactly clear to me what you wanted, but

Felix

> On 5 Mar 2016, at 12:41, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Labeller functions have changed in ggplot2-2.x.y; to see the current
> help page for version 2.1.0, go here:
> http://docs.ggplot2.org/dev/labeller.html
>
> It's not exactly clear to me what you wanted, but if the idea is to
> print "Label" when class = A and "Label 2" when class = B, then this
> works:
>
> library(ggplot2)     # version 2.1.0
> DATA <- structure(list(NO = c(3L, 8L, 2L, 1L), ITEM = structure(1:4,
> .Label = c("W",
> "X", "Y", "Z"), class = "factor"), CLASS = structure(c(1L, 1L,
> 2L, 2L), .Label = c("A", "B"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("NO",
> "ITEM", "CLASS"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -4L
> ))
>
> p <- ggplot(data=DATA, aes(x=ITEM, y =NO))+
>  geom_bar(stat="identity")
>
> # In ggplot v. 2.0.0 +, you can use a labeller function with facet_wrap():
>
> p <- ggplot(data=DATA, aes(x=ITEM, y =NO))+
>  geom_bar(stat="identity")
>
> my_labs <- c(A = "Label", B = "Label 2")
> p + facet_wrap(~ CLASS,
>                      labeller = labeller(CLASS = my_labs),
>                      scales = "free_x")
>
> The functionality for facet labels has changed enough that it's
> probably worth re-educating yourself about its (new) capabilities.
>
> Dennis
>

messages.subject: Controlling legend order when inserting data points from a different data frame
messages.subject_clean: Controlling legend order when inserting data points from a different data frame
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to build a diagram containing a few reference points from a different data frame than my main one. A simplified example illustrating my issue is embedded below: I am plotting the data present in data frame a, but I want to insert a few data points from data frame b.

library(ggplot2)
a = data.frame(val=c(1,2,3,2,4,6),group=c('a','b','c','a','b','c'))
b = data.frame(val=c(2,3,4),group=c('d','e','f'))

a$group = factor(a$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))
b$group = factor(b$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))

p = ggplot(data=a,aes(val,val,color=group,group=group))
p = p + geom_point()
p = p + geom_point(data=b)
p

The problem is that this appears to cause ggplot2 to disregard the order of the factors when building the legend. I can understand that it wouldn't know what to do if data frame b introduced new levels not present in data frame a, but I would have expected that manually specifying all the levels in both data frames, even when they are not all present in either of them, would provide it with the information needed. It appears that this is not the case.

Is there any other way to make the legend entries appear in the order I want them to, rather than the forced alphabetic order they come out now?

b = data.frame(val=c(2,3,4),group=c('d','e','f'))

ab <- bind_rows(a,b)
ab$group <- factor(ab$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))

p = ggplot(data=filter(ab),aes(val,val,color=group,group=group))

p = p + geom_point()
p

So bind them together into one dataframe? The order the factor levels.

HTH,

Sam

messages.body_plain:
All,

I believe a recent upgrade in ggplot2 is affecting the facet labels in ways that I do not know how to control.

I have attached two plots.

“Rplot_numFix_by_Lvl_nc” used:  facet_wrap(crit.sc <http://crit.sc> ~ sid, ncol=5) to produce the label that I like — namely it has both the “crit.sc <http://crit.sc>” and the “sid” in the header of each plot, with a comma btw the two. NOTE THAT THESE ARE ON THE SAME LINE!! That is good!!

Now — look at the “Rplot_new_plot”. You will see that ggplot is putting each of the two values EACH ON ITS OWN LINE — thereby using TWO lines!! I can no longer study the changes over each facet as they are all smooshed! (tech term for the newbies reading this)!

I used to use this:

+  facet_wrap(crit.sc <http://crit.sc> ~ sid, ncol=4)
and it gave me what I wanted, both values on the same line.
BUT now it puts them each on separate line so that the header is wider than the plot!!

I have played with the “new” (???) labeller feature to no avail!

+  facet_wrap(crit.sc <http://crit.sc> ~ sid, ncol=4, labeller = label_value)
## gives exactly the same result as my original command

+  facet_wrap(crit.sc <http://crit.sc> ~ sid, ncol=4, labeller = label_wrap_gen(width=100)  # still two lines

+  facet_wrap(crit.sc <http://crit.sc> ~ sid, ncol=4, labeller = label_value(multi-line = FALSE) # breaks ggplot

Thanks for any help,

Wayne

messages.body_plain:
Hi:

The labeller functions have changed in version 2.x.y. What you need is
the .multi_line = FALSE argument in the revised labeller() function.
Here's an example using the mtcars data:

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = disp, y = mpg)) +
   geom_point() +
   facet_wrap(~ vs + am, label = labeller(.default = label_both,
                                          .multi_line = FALSE))

Since you wanted label_both() for each strip label, I used it as the default.

Dennis

= c("Var1",

3L), dimnames = structure(list(Var1 = c("Var1=a", "Var1=b", "Var1=c"
), Var2 = c("Var2=x", "Var2=y", "Var2=z")), .Names = c("Var1",
"Var2"))), .Names = c("dim", "dimnames")), row.names = c(NA,
-9L), class = "data.frame")

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Below is an example taken from ggplot2’s documentation:

##------------------------------------------------------------------------

## example from http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_density_2d.html

p1 <- ggplot(faithful, aes(x=eruptions, y=waiting)) +

  xlim(0.5, 6) +

  ylim(40, 110) +

  stat_density2d(aes(fill=..level..), geom="polygon") +

  geom_density2d() +

  geom_point()

I am trying to reproduce the same plot following a coding convention I have adopted from http://sape.inf.usi.ch/quick-reference/ggplot2

##------------------------------------------------------------------------

## same plot using adopted coding convention

## axes limits

x.limits <- c(0.5, 6)

y.limits <- c(40, 110)

## initialize plot

p2 <- ggplot() +

  coord_cartesian(xlim=x.limits, ylim=y.limits) +

  scale_x_continuous(name="eruptions") +

  scale_y_continuous(name="waiting")

## plot filled contours

p2 <- p2 +

  layer(

    data=faithful,

    mapping=aes(x=eruptions, y=waiting, fill=..level..),

    stat="density2d",

    geom="polygon",

    geom_params=list(),

    position=position_identity()

  )

## plot contour lines

p2 <- p2 +

  layer(

    data=faithful,

    mapping=aes(x=eruptions, y=waiting),

    stat="density2d",

    geom="density2d",

    geom_params=list(),

    position=position_identity()

  )

## plot data points

p2 <- p2 +

  layer(

    data=faithful,

    mapping=aes(x=eruptions, y=waiting),

    stat="identity",

    geom="point",

    geom_params=list(),

    position=position_identity()

  )

p2 doesn’t quite come out like p1 and I am wondering what is missing in my version of the code to achieve the same result.

Thanks in advance.

Benoit Casault

messages.subject: clipping a shapefile in ggmap
messages.subject_clean: clipping a shapefile in ggmap
messages.body_plain:
Dear friends,

For days now I am trying to clip a shapefile in ggmap.  I have the shapefile for the Hydrographic Areas in Clark County, NV (Clark county HA.png).  I need to zoom in and look at a specific area in detail, here is my “box”: ylim=c(36.3,36.65) and xlim=c(-115.2,-114.7).   I can extract the area, but have some additional  straight lines because the shp-file is not clipped (properly).  My result is captured in sourcesSatellitte.png.

Hopefully you can provide some help.

Here is my code so far:

library(ggmap)

library(mapproj)

library(ggplot2)

library(maps)

library(rgdal)

######## read shapefile #########

HA <- readOGR("q:/HA", "cntyhb_p")

HA <- spTransform(HA, CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84"))

HA <- fortify(HA)

####### extract map ##############

map = get_map(location =  c(lon = -114.96, lat = 36.46), zoom = 11,maptype = "satellite",color="bw")

map = ggmap(map,extent="device")

map

map<-map + geom_polygon(aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group), fill='grey', size=1,color='black', data=HA, alpha=0) +coord_fixed(ylim=c(36.3,36.65),xlim=c(-115.2,-114.7),ratio=1.3/1)

#png("q:/sourcesSatellite.png", width = 7,height =7, res =300,units="in")

map

#dev.off()

Thanks,

Jean-Paul Huys

messages.subject: Re: clipping a shapefile in ggmap
messages.subject_clean: clipping a shapefile in ggmap
messages.body_plain:
Jean-Paul--
You may need to clip your shapefile explicitly first.   There are several threads on clipping SpatialPolygonsDataFrame objects to a bounding box while retaining the attributes.  One is at:
http://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/46954/clip-spatial-object-to-bounding-box-in-r
https://gist.github.com/yapweiliang/9e066a6369a242fb3aef

My version (which accepts a bounding box 2x2 matrix from bbox or xmin xmax ymin ymax):
require(raster) # for extent
gClip <- function(shp, bb, keep.attribs=TRUE) {
    if(class(bb) == "matrix") bb <- as.vector(t(bb))
    b_poly <- as(extent(bb), "SpatialPolygons")
    if (is.na <http://is.na>(proj4string(b_poly))) {
        cat('Missing CRS on Bounding Box, using CRS of shp\n')
        proj4string(b_poly) <- CRS(proj4string(shp))
    } # if is.na <http://is.na>(proj4string
    new.shape <- gIntersection(shp, b_poly, byid = T)
    if(keep.attribs){
        new.attribs <- data.frame(do.call(rbind,strsplit(row.names(new.shape)," ")),stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        new.attrib.data <- shp[new.attribs$X1,]@data
        row.names(new.shape) <- row.names(new.attrib.data)
        return(SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(new.shape, new.attrib.data))
    }else {
        return(new.shape)
    }
} # bottom function gClip

My example call:
IUCN.BatPoly <- gClip(IUCN.BatPoly,c(-168,-60,15.5,70))

Tom 2

Jean-Paul--

You may need to clip your shapefile explicitly first.   There are several threads on clipping SpatialPolygonsDataFrame objects to a bounding box while retaining the attributes.  One is at:

http://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/46954/clip-spatial-object-to-bounding-box-in-r

https://gist.github.com/yapweiliang/9e066a6369a242fb3aef

My version (which accepts a bounding box 2x2 matrix from bbox or xmin xmax ymin ymax):

require(raster) # for extent

gClip <- function(shp, bb, keep.attribs=TRUE) {

    if(class(bb) == "matrix") bb <- as.vector(t(bb))

    b_poly <- as(extent(bb), "SpatialPolygons")

    if (is.na <http://is.na>(proj4string(b_poly))) {

        cat('Missing CRS on Bounding Box, using CRS of shp\n')

        proj4string(b_poly) <- CRS(proj4string(shp))

    } # if is.na <http://is.na>(proj4string

    new.shape <- gIntersection(shp, b_poly, byid = T)

    if(keep.attribs){

        new.attribs <- data.frame(do.call(rbind,strsplit(row.names(new.shape)," ")),stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

        new.attrib.data <- shp[new.attribs$X1,]@data

        row.names(new.shape) <- row.names(new.attrib.data)

        return(SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(new.shape, new.attrib.data))

    }else {

        return(new.shape)

    }

} # bottom function gClip

My example call:

IUCN.BatPoly <- gClip(IUCN.BatPoly,c(-168,-60,15.5,70))

Tom 2

The data set I’m using is composed of units sold of different products manufactured for different brands in a market. Units sold for each product are reported monthly. I have fields for Product#, Brand, Month, Year and Units Sold.

I'm trying to create a stacked bar chart for total units sold by brands in the market by year. The X axis should represent the year (ex. 2012, 2013, etc.) The Y axis should represent total units sold. Each bar should be composed of the units sold for each brand in market with the height segments in the bar representing the units sales for brands in a year and the total number of units sold for the year represented by the cumulative height of the bar for year. The data contains negative, positive, and zero values for units sold (This is due to returns and credits). Total units sold in per year and for each brand yearly should be the sum of the units sold.

I’m using the following code:

##Load ggplot2 package from library for data visualization

messages.body_plain:
I have a guess:
Do you perhaps have 12 bars of each color in each stack?
In order to generate graphs with annual values, you have to give ggplot data with annual values.
Try using aggregate or the plyr equivalent to generate a dataset of Product#, Brand, Year and Units Sold.

And the error message is pretty valid: how would you want to have a bar of negative height displayed in a stacked bar chart?  There is no single right answer (ignoring whether stacked bar charts are a right answer in the first place).  One _might_ stick negative bars below the 0 value, so that the bar height above 0 is the net total, but then your bar / stack order varies across years.  Is your stack order meaningful?  These are more visualization issues than R or ggplot issues.

I hope that this helps...

Tom 2
